title: A qubit trine obstructs a universal three-source balanced entropy transfer
status_authority: The exact source scope and version-bound receiving review are recorded below; this card does not certify priority, physical operation, or practical advantage.
reported_status: The recipient checked the selected trine and scalar-entropy source passages at the exact scope below. No full-package audit, separate binary producer audit, producer-script replay, external priority review, or physical/practical validation is asserted.

proof_availability.classification_scope: The scalar balanced third finite difference s(a+b+c)-s(a+b)-s(a+c)-s(b+c)+s(a)+s(b)+s(c), for s(t)=-t log t, is nonnegative for all a,b,c>=0. For the three real qubit trine projectors P_0,P_1,P_2, the corresponding balanced matrix trace-entropy expression is (3/2)log(3/4)<0, since the sum has spectrum (3/2,3/2), each pair has spectrum (3/2,1/2), and each individual projector has spectrum (1,0). The scalar-to-matrix transfer therefore fails in this explicit three-source case, and negativity persists under sufficiently small positive epsilon-identity perturbations. Boundary: This is an obstruction to one universal balanced three-source entropy lift. It is not a W3 counterexample, does not contradict the older arbitrary-classical-channel/qubit-reference global mutual-information theorem, and does not establish a t log t fixed-prior matrix-SDPI separation.
